proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a support rule \(s\), a feasible weight array \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), and
\(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  Put \(t=T_j+h\) and
\[
 d_e(w)=x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i.
 \tag{1}
\]
The simplex constraint in the definition of \(\mathcal F_s\) gives
\(w_{jh,i}\geq0\), \(\sum_iw_{jh,i}=1\), and zero weight outside the
applicable donor set.  For the deep rule this support is also contained in
\(D_{jh}\), because \(h\leq K\) implies
\(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\).  Thus the definition of \(a_e(w)\) and
\texttt{ass:mean-structure} give, equation by equation,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 a_e(w)^{\top}m
 &=m_{jt}-\sum_iw_{jh,i}m_{it}\\
 &=x_j^{\top}\beta_t+r_{jt}
   -\sum_iw_{jh,i}(x_i^{\top}\beta_t+r_{it})\\
 &=d_e(w)^{\top}\beta_t+r_{jt}-\sum_iw_{jh,i}r_{it}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
By Cauchy--Schwarz, \texttt{ass:coefficient-radius},
\texttt{ass:cellwise-misspecification}, nonnegativity of the weights, and
their unit sum,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |a_e(w)^{\top}m|
 &\leq \lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2\lVert\beta_t\rVert_2
       +|r_{jt}|+\sum_iw_{jh,i}|r_{it}|\\
 &\leq L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\frac{\delta}{2}
       +\frac{\delta}{2}\sum_iw_{jh,i}\\
 &=L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2+\delta
 =b_e(w).
\end{aligned}
\tag{3}
\]

It remains to show that (3) is the exact support function, rather than only
an upper bound.  For \(\eta\in\{-1,1\}\), define the coefficient vector at
time \(t\) by
\[
 \beta_t^{(\eta)}=
 \begin{cases}
 \displaystyle \eta L\,d_e(w)/\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2,
     &d_e(w)\neq0,\\[3pt]
 0,&d_e(w)=0,
 \end{cases}
 \tag{4}
\]
and put \(\beta_{t'}^{(\eta)}=0\) for \(t'\neq t\).  Set
\[
 r_{jt}^{(\eta)}=\eta\frac{\delta}{2},
 \qquad
 r_{it}^{(\eta)}=-\eta\frac{\delta}{2}
 \quad\hbox{when }w_{jh,i}>0,
 \tag{5}
\]
and set all remaining remainder coordinates equal to zero.  These assignments
are compatible on the deduplicated cell set: every positively weighted donor
satisfies \(T_i>t\), whereas \(T_j\leq t\), so no donor cell
\((i,t)\) in (5) is the focal cell \((j,t)\).  Equations (4)--(5) satisfy
the coefficient and cellwise bounds, including the boundary cases \(L=0\)
and \(\delta=0\).  Defining \(m^{(\eta)}\) by
\texttt{ass:mean-structure} and substituting in (2) yields
\[
 a_e(w)^{\top}m^{(\eta)}
 =\eta L\lVert d_e(w)\rVert_2
   +\eta\frac{\delta}{2}
   +\eta\frac{\delta}{2}\sum_iw_{jh,i}
 =\eta b_e(w).
 \tag{6}
\]

For completeness, each mean in (6) is realized by a law, not merely by a
formal nuisance assignment.  On the fixed inputs defining
\(\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}(L,\delta,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max})\), take
\(Q\sim N(m^{(\eta)},\Sigma_Q)\), use its deduplicated coordinates as the
untreated potential outcomes on \(\mathcal C\), extend the untreated array
arbitrarily outside \(\mathcal C\), choose arbitrary treated potential
outcomes, and define observed outcomes by \texttt{ass:consistency}.  The mean
conditions hold by (4)--(5), the Gaussian condition holds by construction,
and the fixed covariance obeys the covariance-band condition required in
\texttt{def:model-class}.  Hence this is a member of that class.  Taking
\(\eta=1\) and \(\eta=-1\) proves attainability of both endpoints in (6).
Together with (3), this proves
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}
 |a_e(w)^{\top}m|=b_e(w).
\]
No limiting argument is used.

Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\), and for
\(w\in\mathcal F_s\) define
\[
 H_s(w)=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \{b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}.
 \tag{1}
\]
The condition \texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} makes every deepest donor set
\(D_{jK}\) nonempty.  Since \(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\) for
\(0\leq h\leq K\), every simplex occurring under either support rule is
nonempty.  Each is compact, and \(\mathcal E\) is finite.  Therefore
\(\mathcal F_s\) is a nonempty compact finite product of simplexes.  The
two norms defining \(b_e(w)\) and \(\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\) are continuous
norms of affine functions of \(w\); hence \(H_s\) is continuous and attains
its minimum.

The program in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} is exactly an epigraph form of
that minimum.  Indeed, every feasible \((w,u,v,g)\) satisfies, for every
\(e=(j,h)\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)
 &=L\left\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\rVert_2+
   \delta+z_B\lVert R_Qa_e(w)\rVert_2\\
 &\leq Lu_e+\delta+z_Bv_e
 \leq g.
\end{aligned}
\tag{2}
\]
Conversely, for any \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), the choices
\[
 u_e=\left\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 v_e=\lVert R_Qa_e(w)\rVert_2,
 \qquad
 g=H_s(w)
 \tag{3}
\]
are feasible.  Consequently,
\[
 \Gamma_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}H_s(w).
 \tag{4}
\]
In particular an optimizer exists, and if \((w,u,v,g)\) is any optimizer,
then (2)--(4) imply \(H_s(w)=g=\Gamma_s\).  Thus the maximum of the actual
half-widths in the statement, rather than of possibly slack auxiliary
variables, equals \(\Gamma_s\).

Now fix any such optimizing weight array and any
\(P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}(L,\delta,\sigma_{\min},\sigma_{\max})\).
By \texttt{lem:prediction-error} and \texttt{lem:bias-radius}, jointly over
\(e\in\mathcal E\),
\[
 \widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e=\mu_e+Z_e,
 \qquad
 \mu_e=a_e(w)^{\top}m,
 \qquad
 |\mu_e|\leq b_e(w),
 \tag{5}
\]
where \(Z\) is centered Gaussian with covariance
\(A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}\).  The row \(a_e(w)\) is nonzero because its
focal coordinate equals one, and \(R_Q\) has full rank.  Hence
\(\operatorname{sd}_e(w)=\lVert R_Qa_e(w)\rVert_2>0\), and
\(Z_e/\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\sim N(0,1)\).

Consider the event
\[
 \mathcal G=
 \bigcap_{e\in\mathcal E}
 \{|Z_e|\leq z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}.
 \tag{6}
\]
On \(\mathcal G\), the triangle inequality and (5) give, simultaneously for
all coordinates,
\[
 |\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|
 \leq b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w).
 \tag{7}
\]
No independence is required.  The union bound, the fact that
\(M=|\mathcal E|\), and the first outward-rounded certificate in the
definition of \(z_B\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P(\mathcal G^c)
 &\leq\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}
       P\{|Z_e|>z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}\\
 &=2M\{1-\Phi(z_B)\}
 \leq\alpha.
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
Combining (7)--(8) proves simultaneous coverage at least \(1-\alpha\).
The argument is finite-sample and uniform because the only law-dependent
mean quantity in (5) is bounded by the exact model-class support function.

Finally, the record in \texttt{def:finite-input} has rational scalar and
matrix entries.  For each \(e=(j,h)\), the two norm constraints are precisely
\[
 \left(u_{jh},x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right)\in\mathcal L_{p+1},
 \qquad
 (v_{jh},R_Qa_{jh}(w))\in\mathcal L_{|\mathcal C|+1}.
 \tag{9}
\]
The simplex restrictions and the epigraph inequalities are rational linear
equalities plus nonnegative slacks.  Splitting each free scalar into positive
and negative parts and retaining equalities in zero-cone blocks therefore
gives exactly the rational product-cone record of
\texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}.  Conversely, recombining split
variables and eliminating slacks recovers (2) and the simplex constraints,
so the encoding preserves the feasible objective values in both directions.
Its value is therefore \(\Gamma_s\) by (4), which completes the proof.

Fix \(s\in\{\mathrm{nested},\mathrm{deep}\}\).  By
\texttt{thm:socp-coverage}, an optimizing SOCP weight array together with
the deterministic half-widths
\[
 \ell_e=b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)
 \tag{1}
\]
is feasible for the honest-band problem in
\texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}, and its maximum half-width is
\(\Gamma_s\).  Therefore
\[
 W_s\leq\Gamma_s.
 \tag{2}
\]

For the reverse comparison, take an arbitrary feasible pair \((w,\ell)\)
in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} and put
\[
 R=\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e.
 \tag{3}
\]
The standing condition \(\mathcal J\neq\varnothing\), together with
\(K\geq0\), implies \(M=|\mathcal E|\geq1\), so the maximum in (3) and
\(q_\alpha(M)\) are well defined.

We first prove a deterministic bias lower bound.  Suppose for contradiction
that \(b_e(w)>R\) for some coordinate \(e\).  By
\texttt{lem:bias-radius}, there is a law \(P_e\) in the model class under
which the mean of the coordinate error is \(b_e(w)\).  Its variance is
\(\operatorname{sd}_e(w)^2>0\), by
\texttt{lem:contrast-geometry}.  Writing the coordinate error as
\(b_e(w)+\operatorname{sd}_e(w)G\), where \(G\sim N(0,1)\), and using
\(\ell_e\leq R<b_e(w)\), we obtain
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P_e\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e\}
 &\leq P_e\{\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e\leq\ell_e\}\\
 &=\Phi\!\left(
    \frac{\ell_e-b_e(w)}{\operatorname{sd}_e(w)}\right)
 <\frac12.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
The simultaneous coverage probability is no larger than this marginal
probability.  Equation (4) contradicts uniform coverage at least
\(1-\alpha>1/2\).  Hence
\[
 \max_{e\in\mathcal E}b_e(w)\leq R.
 \tag{5}
\]

We next prove the stochastic lower bound without imposing independence on the
actual contrasts.  Choose any \(e_0\in\mathcal E\).  The endpoint-attainment
part of \texttt{lem:bias-radius} supplies at least one model-class law
\(P_0\).  Under this law, \texttt{lem:prediction-error} represents the full
error vector as
\[
 \widehat\tau(w)-\tau=\mu+Z,
 \qquad
 Z\sim N(0,V),
 \qquad
 V=A(w)\Sigma_QA(w)^{\top}.
 \tag{6}
\]
By \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry},
\[
 V\succeq\sigma_{\min}I_M.
 \tag{7}
\]
Set \(C=V-\sigma_{\min}I_M\succeq0\).  A spectral decomposition of \(C\)
constructs a possibly singular Gaussian vector \(U\sim N(0,C)\).  On a
product probability space, take it independent of
\(X\sim N(0,\sigma_{\min}I_M)\).  Then \(X+U\) has covariance \(V\), so it
has the same centered Gaussian law as \(Z\).

Write \(s_0=\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}>0\).  For \(R>0\) and \(u\in\mathbb R\),
define
\[
 g_R(u)=P\{|s_0G+u|\leq R\}
 =\Phi\!\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)
  +\Phi\!\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)-1.
 \tag{8}
\]
This function is even.  For \(u\geq0\), differentiation gives
\[
 g_R'(u)=\frac1{s_0}\left\{
 \varphi\!\left(\frac{R+u}{s_0}\right)
 -\varphi\!\left(\frac{R-u}{s_0}\right)\right\}\leq0,
 \tag{9}
\]
because \(|R+u|\geq|R-u|\) and the standard normal density is decreasing
as a function of absolute value.  Thus \(g_R(u)\leq g_R(0)\) for every real
\(u\).  Conditional on \(U=u\), the coordinates of \(X\) are independent;
therefore (8)--(9), applied with the deterministic shifts \(u_k+\mu_k\),
give
\[
\begin{aligned}
 P\{\mu+X+U\in[-R,R]^M\mid U=u\}
 &=\prod_{k=1}^M g_R(u_k+\mu_k)\\
 &\leq g_R(0)^M
 =P\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Integration over the possibly degenerate law of \(U\) proves the same
inequality unconditionally.  For \(R=0\), both cube probabilities involving
the nonsingular vector \(X\) are zero, so the inequality also holds at the
boundary.

The coverage rectangle for \((w,\ell)\) is contained in \([-R,R]^M\).
Applying honesty under the particular law \(P_0\), then (6) and (10), gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 1-\alpha
 &\leq P_0\{|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e|\leq\ell_e
              \text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E\}\\
 &\leq P_0\{\widehat\tau(w)-\tau\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
 &\leq P\{X\in[-R,R]^M\}\\
 &=P\left\{\max_{1\leq k\leq M}|G_k|
       \leq\frac{R}{\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}}\right\},
\end{aligned}
\tag{11}
\]
where the \(G_k\) in the last line are independent standard normals.  The
right side of (11) is zero at \(R=0\) and is strictly increasing in its
nonnegative threshold.  The definition of \(q_\alpha(M)\) therefore yields
\[
 R\geq\sqrt{\sigma_{\min}}\,q_\alpha(M).
 \tag{12}
\]

By the coordinate upper bound in \texttt{lem:contrast-geometry} and by
\texttt{lem:gaussian-quantile-ratio}, respectively,
\[
 \operatorname{sd}_e(w)\leq\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}
 \quad(e\in\mathcal E),
 \qquad
 z_B\leq c_\alpha q_\alpha(M).
 \tag{13}
\]
Using (5), (12), and (13) in the variational characterization of
\(\Gamma_s\) proved in \texttt{thm:socp-coverage} gives
\[
\begin{aligned}
 \Gamma_s
 &\leq\max_{e\in\mathcal E}
       \{b_e(w)+z_B\operatorname{sd}_e(w)\}\\
 &\leq R+c_\alpha q_\alpha(M)\sqrt{2\sigma_{\max}}\\
 &\leq\left(1+c_\alpha
       \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)R.
\end{aligned}
\tag{14}
\]
The feasible pair \((w,\ell)\) was arbitrary.  Taking its infimum in (14),
as prescribed by \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}, and combining with (2)
proves
\[
 W_s\leq\Gamma_s\leq
 \left(1+c_\alpha
 \sqrt{\frac{2\sigma_{\max}}{\sigma_{\min}}}\right)W_s.
\]
The denominator is positive by the declared covariance-band parameter domain.
There is no asymptotic or limit condition.  The multiplier depends only on
the fixed \(\alpha\) and covariance-band ratio, and hence not on any of the
dimensions, adoption pattern, predictors, or donor-overlap geometry listed
in the claim.

Assume \(M=1\), \(\delta=0\), and let the selected feasible simplex weight
\(w\) exactly balance the predictors, so that
\[
 x_j-\sum_iw_ix_i=0.
 \tag{1}
\]
The definition of the exact bias radius gives
\[
 b(w)=L\left\lVert x_j-\sum_iw_ix_i\right\rVert_2+\delta=0.
 \tag{2}
\]
Substitution of (2) into the band formula in
\texttt{thm:socp-coverage} leaves
\[
 \widehat\tau(w)\ \pm\ z_B\operatorname{sd}(w).
 \tag{3}
\]
Because \(R_Q\) is full rank and the focal coefficient of the contrast is
one, \(\operatorname{sd}(w)>0\).  Thus (3) is precisely the usual
known-covariance Gaussian interval form, with the supplied certified
critical value.  No misspecification or predictor-imbalance term remains.

It remains to prove the approximation assertion about certified rational
multipliers.  Put
\[
 z_\star=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
 \tag{4}
\]
Since \(0<\alpha<1/2\), one has \(1-\alpha/2>1/2\), and hence
\(z_\star>0\).  Let \(\varepsilon>0\).  Density of the rationals in the
reals gives a positive \(q\in\mathbb Q\) such that
\[
 z_\star<q<z_\star+\min\{\varepsilon,1\}.
 \tag{5}
\]
Strict monotonicity of the normal distribution function and (4)--(5) imply
\[
 2\{1-\Phi(q)\}<\alpha,
 \qquad
 q<\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)+1.
 \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(q\) satisfies both strict inequalities required of \(z_B\) when
\(M=1\), and \(0<q-z_\star<\varepsilon\).

We finally verify that the word ``certified'' in the claim imposes no hidden
analytic assumption.  For every nonnegative rational \(y\),
\[
 \Phi(y)=\frac12+\frac1{\sqrt{2\pi}}
             \int_0^y e^{-u^2/2}\,du.
 \tag{7}
\]
The identity
\(\pi=16\arctan(1/5)-4\arctan(1/239)\), together with the alternating
rational power series for \(\arctan\), gives nested rational intervals for
\(\pi\) whose widths tend to zero.  Rational bisection and reciprocation then
give such intervals for \((2\pi)^{-1/2}\).  On the rational compact interval
\([0,y]\), truncating the Taylor polynomial of \(e^{-v}\) after degree
\(n\) has remainder bounded in absolute value by
\(v^{n+1}/(n+1)!\).  Substituting \(v=u^2/2\), integrating the rational
polynomial, and integrating this uniform rational remainder bound gives
outward rational lower and upper bounds for the integral in (7), with width
tending to zero.  Hence \(\Phi(y)\) admits arbitrarily sharp, finite,
outward-rounded rational certificates.

Apply this construction at \(y=q\).  The first strict gap in (6) ensures
that a sufficiently refined lower bound for \(\Phi(q)\) certifies
\(2\{1-\Phi(q)\}<\alpha\).  For the second inequality, if \(q\leq1\), it
follows immediately from \(z_\star>0\).  If \(q>1\), (5) gives
\(q-1<z_\star\), equivalently
\[
 \Phi(q-1)<1-\alpha/2,
\]
and a sufficiently refined upper rational bound at the nonnegative rational
argument \(q-1\) certifies this strict inequality.  Thus both certificates
are finite and outward rounded.  Since \(\varepsilon\) was arbitrary,
certified rational choices of \(z_B\) approach
\(\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2)\) arbitrarily closely from above.

Fix an admissible design and a coordinate \(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E\).  By the definition of \(\mathcal E\), \(0\leq h\leq K\).  If \(i\in D_{jK}\), then the definition of the donor sets gives
\[
 T_i>T_j+K\geq T_j+h,
\]
so \(i\in D_{jh}\).  Hence
\[
 D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}
 \qquad\text{for every }(j,h)\in\mathcal E. \tag{1}
\]
Assumption \texttt{ass:donor-feasibility} ensures that \(D_{jK}\) is nonempty.  Let \(q\in\Delta(D_{jK})\).  Then \(q_i\geq0\) for every \(i\), \(q_i=0\) for \(i\notin D_{jK}\), and \(\sum_{i\in D_{jK}}q_i=1\).  By (1), \(q_i=0\) for every \(i\in D_{jh}\setminus D_{jK}\) as well as for every \(i\notin D_{jh}\), and therefore
\[
 \sum_{i\in D_{jh}}q_i
 =\sum_{i\in D_{jK}}q_i
  +\sum_{i\in D_{jh}\setminus D_{jK}}q_i
 =1.
\]
Thus \(q\in\Delta(D_{jh})\), proving
\[
 \Delta(D_{jK})\subseteq\Delta(D_{jh})
 \qquad(e=(j,h)\in\mathcal E). \tag{2}
\]
Taking the product of (2) over the finite coordinate set \(\mathcal E\), according to the definition of \(\mathcal F_s\), yields
\[
 \mathcal F_{\mathrm{deep}}
 =\prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jK})
 \subseteq
 \prod_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}\Delta(D_{jh})
 =\mathcal F_{\mathrm{nested}}. \tag{3}
\]

For the exact frontier, let \(\mathcal H_s\) be the set of all pairs \((w,\ell)\) feasible in \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier} under support rule \(s\).  Apart from the condition \(w\in\mathcal F_s\), all requirements defining \(\mathcal H_s\) are identical for the two rules: \(\ell\in[0,\infty)^M\); both \(w\) and \(\ell\) depend only on the fixed inputs; and
\[
 \inf_{P\in\mathcal M_{N,T,K,p}}
 P\!\left(
   \left|\widehat\tau_e(w)-\tau_e\right|\leq\ell_e
   \text{ for every }e\in\mathcal E
 \right)\geq1-\alpha. \tag{4}
\]
In particular, neither the model class, the target \(\tau\), the estimator evaluated at a fixed numerical weight array, nor condition (4) changes when that same array is regarded as nested-feasible.  Consequently, (3) implies
\[
 \mathcal H_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal H_{\mathrm{nested}}. \tag{5}
\]
The objective \((w,\ell)\mapsto\max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e\) is also common to the two problems.  Monotonicity of the infimum under the feasible-set inclusion (5), applied to \texttt{def:exact-width-frontier}, gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 W_{\mathrm{nested}}
 &=\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{nested}}}
       \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e \\
 &\leq\inf_{(w,\ell)\in\mathcal H_{\mathrm{deep}}}
       \max_{e\in\mathcal E}\ell_e
 =W_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{6}
 \end{aligned}
\]
This comparison also covers an empty honesty-feasible set under the extended-value convention \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\) used by the codomain of \(W_s\).

For the conic frontier, let \(\mathcal S_s\) be the feasible set of quadruples \((w,u,v,g)\) in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp}.  If \((w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}\), then (3) makes \(w\) nested-feasible.  Moreover, for each \(e=(j,h)\), the coordinates of this deep-feasible \(w_e\) outside \(D_{jK}\) vanish.  Since \(D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}\), the predictor sum \(\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\) and the deduplicated contrast row \(a_{jh}(w)\) have exactly the same numerical values when \(w\) is viewed as an element of either feasible set.  Thus each of the common constraints
\[
 \left\|x_j-\sum_iw_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2\leq u_{jh},
 \qquad
 \left\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right\|_2\leq v_{jh},
 \qquad
 Lu_{jh}+\delta+z_Bv_{jh}\leq g \tag{7}
\]
remains satisfied.  It follows that
\[
 \mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}\subseteq\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}. \tag{8}
\]
The scalar objective \(g\) is the same in both programs.  Therefore (8) and the minimizations in \texttt{def:bonferroni-socp} imply
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 =\min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{nested}}}g
 \leq
 \min_{(w,u,v,g)\in\mathcal S_{\mathrm{deep}}}g
 =\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{9}
\]
Equations (6) and (9) prove both asserted boundary inequalities.

Let a valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) be given, and put
\[
 p_N:=c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N,
 \qquad
 q_D:=d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D.
\]
By \texttt{def:gap-certificate},
\[
 B_{\mathrm{nested}}y_N=d_{\mathrm{nested}},
 \qquad y_N\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{nested}}.
\]
Thus \(y_N\) is feasible for the nested standard-form program of
\texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}.  Since that program has value
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\), weak minimization gives
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}\leq p_N. \tag{1}
\]

We next verify explicitly that every feasible vector of the original deep
program lies in the terminal face recorded by the certificate.  Let \(y\)
satisfy
\[
 B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}},
 \qquad y\in\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}=F_0.
\]
Suppose inductively that \(y\in F_{k-1}\).  The exposing identities in
\texttt{def:facial-dual} give
\[
 z_k=B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k,
 \qquad d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k=0,
 \qquad F_k=F_{k-1}\cap z_k^\perp.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 z_k^{\top}y
 =\eta_k^{\top}B_{\mathrm{deep}}y
 =\eta_k^{\top}d_{\mathrm{deep}}
 =0,
\]
so \(y\in F_k\).  Induction yields
\[
 y\in F_r=F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{2}
\]
The certificate's relative-interior point \(y^\circ\) also shows that the
deep feasible set is nonempty.

The facial-dual part of \texttt{def:gap-certificate} gives
\[
 s_D:=c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
 \in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*.
\]
For every deep feasible \(y\), (2), the definition of the dual cone, and the
deep affine equality imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}y-q_D
 &=\bigl(c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D\bigr)^{\top}y
   +\lambda_D^{\top}
      \bigl(B_{\mathrm{deep}}y-d_{\mathrm{deep}}\bigr)\\
 &=s_D^{\top}y\geq0.
 \end{aligned} \tag{3}
\]
Taking the infimum in (3), and using the objective-preserving encoding in
\texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}, gives the facial-dual weak bound
\[
 q_D\leq\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{4}
\]
This step uses only membership in the terminal face and its dual; it does not
use ordinary Slater feasibility, strict complementarity, or an optimizer-rank
condition.

Finally, the two certified interval inclusions in
\texttt{def:gap-certificate} and their strict separation give
\[
 p_N\leq\sup I_N<\inf I_D\leq q_D. \tag{5}
\]
Combining (1), (5), and (4) yields
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}
 \leq p_N<q_D
 \leq\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
\]
and hence
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}\).
All affine equalities and cone memberships used above are exact algebraic
relations.  Outward rational rounding occurs only in the enclosures in (5).
The proof therefore remains valid when a donor weight is zero, an affine
constraint is redundant, or an orthant or Lorentz block lies in a proper
face.

Write \(P_s\) for the standard-form program in
\texttt{def:standard-conic-encoding}, and interpret its value in
\([0,+\infty]\).  We first settle feasibility and attainment, including the
boundary case in which a donor simplex is empty.

For \(0\leq h\leq K\), the definition of the donor sets gives
\[
 D_{jK}\subseteq D_{jh}, \tag{6}
\]
because \(T_i>T_j+K\) implies \(T_i>T_j+h\).  If the nested program is
feasible, then its horizon-\(K\) coordinate supplies an element of
\(\Delta(D_{jK})\) for every \(j\in\mathcal J\), so each \(D_{jK}\) is
nonempty.  Choosing one point of each such simplex at every horizon gives a
deep-feasible weight array.  Conversely, (6) embeds every deep-feasible
weight array into the nested feasible set.  All norm epigraphs admit finite
slacks once weights have been chosen.  Hence
\[
 P_{\mathrm{nested}}\text{ is feasible}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 P_{\mathrm{deep}}\text{ is feasible}. \tag{7}
\]
If these programs are infeasible, both values are \(+\infty\), so their
strict inequality is false.  A valid \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) is also impossible:
its \(y_N\) would be nested feasible and its \(y^\circ\) would be deep
feasible.  Thus the asserted equivalence already holds in the infeasible
case.

Suppose henceforth that the equivalent conditions in (7) hold.  Eliminating
the norm epigraph variables at a fixed weight array gives
\[
 G_s(w):=\max_{(j,h)\in\mathcal E}
 \left\{
 L\left\|x_j-\sum_i w_{jh,i}x_i\right\|_2
 +\delta+z_B\left\|R_Qa_{jh}(w)\right\|_2
 \right\}. \tag{8}
\]
Indeed, the smallest feasible values of \(u_{jh}\) and \(v_{jh}\) are the
two norms in (8), and the smallest feasible \(g\) is their displayed finite
maximum.  Every nonempty finite-dimensional donor simplex is compact, so the
finite product \(\mathcal F_s\) is compact.  The affine maps, Euclidean
norms, and finite maximum in (8) are continuous.  Therefore
\[
 \Gamma_s=\min_{w\in\mathcal F_s}G_s(w)<+\infty, \tag{9}
\]
and the minimum is attained.  Choosing the norm values, the maximizing
epigraph value, and the corresponding nonnegative slacks restores an
attained optimizer of \(P_s\).  This argument neither requires a unique
minimizer nor divides by a donor weight or a predictor Gram matrix.

Assume first that
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}<\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
 \qquad
 \Delta:=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}-\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}>0. \tag{10}
\]
By (9), choose a nested primal optimizer \(y_N^*\).  The cone
\(\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\) is a finite product of closed orthants,
Lorentz cones, and zero cones, and hence is a finite-dimensional closed
convex cone.  Its affine space
\[
 H_D:=\{y:B_{\mathrm{deep}}y=d_{\mathrm{deep}}\}
\]
meets the cone by (7).  Apply
\texttt{lem:facial-reduction-relative-strong-duality} to this conic affine
system.  It gives a finite strict facial-reduction chain
\[
 \mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}=F_0\supsetneq F_1\supsetneq\cdots
 \supsetneq F_r=F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}, \tag{11}
\]
and a point
\[
 y^\circ\in H_D\cap\operatorname{ri}F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{12}
\]
Each strict inclusion lowers dimension, so
\(r\leq\dim\mathcal K_{\mathrm{deep}}\leq d\).

For completeness, the affine multiplier form required by
\texttt{def:facial-dual} follows by elementary finite-dimensional linear
algebra.  At step \(k\), the orthogonal exposing functional \(z_k\)
annihilates the affine space \(H_D\); in particular it annihilates its
direction space \(\ker B_{\mathrm{deep}}\).  Hence
\[
 z_k\in(\ker B_{\mathrm{deep}})^\perp
       =\operatorname{range}(B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}),
\]
so \(z_k=B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta_k\) for some \(\eta_k\).  For any
\(y_0\in H_D\), annihilation of the affine space then gives
\[
 0=z_k^{\top}y_0
   =\eta_k^{\top}B_{\mathrm{deep}}y_0
   =\eta_k^{\top}d_{\mathrm{deep}}.
\]
Thus the chain satisfies every exposing identity in
\texttt{def:facial-dual}.  Since the deep value is finite by (9), the same
cited lemma supplies an attained facial-dual optimizer \(\lambda_D^*\) with
\[
 c_{\mathrm{deep}}-B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
 \in F_{\min,\mathrm{deep}}^*,
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D^*
 =\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}. \tag{13}
\]

We next show that the real objects in (11)--(13) can be replaced by exact
real-algebraic objects through a terminating procedure, without imposing a
nondegeneracy condition.  The required cone and face relations are
semialgebraic.  Orthant membership is a list of linear weak inequalities, a
zero cone is specified by linear equalities, and
\[
 (t,z)\in\mathcal L_q
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 t\geq0\ \text{ and }\ t^2-\sum_{\nu=1}^{q-1}z_\nu^2\geq0. \tag{14}
\]
The faces of an orthant are its coordinate faces.  A proper nonzero face of a
Lorentz cone is a ray: two noncollinear nonzero boundary points have an
interior midpoint by the strict triangle inequality, and a face containing
an interior point is the whole cone.  Finally, every face of a product cone
is a product of faces.  To see this last assertion, decompose a point of the
face into its block-supported cone components; the face property puts every
component in the face, and closure under addition gives the converse product
inclusion.  Thus an orthant face is encoded by zero/free coordinate labels,
and a Lorentz face is encoded as full, zero, or a ray with a normalized
boundary generator.  Membership, relative-interior membership, dual-face
membership, and equality
\(F_k=F_{k-1}\cap z_k^\perp\) are consequently finite Boolean combinations
of polynomial sign conditions.  Binary labels can themselves be imposed by
\(e(e-1)=0\), so no enumeration of exponentially many cases is required.

For each \(0\leq r\leq d\), form the following first-order formula
\(\Psi_r\) over the rationals.  Its existential variables are a chain of
length \(r\), its face parameters and exposing multipliers, a point
\(y^\circ\) satisfying (12), a nested feasible point \(y_N\), and a feasible
facial-dual point \(\lambda_D\).  Its conditions are exactly those in
\texttt{def:facial-dual}, together with
\[
 \begin{split}
 &c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N
   \leq c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}\widetilde y_N
   \quad\text{for every nested-feasible }\widetilde y_N,\\
 &d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
   \geq d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\widetilde\lambda_D
   \quad\text{for every facial-dual-feasible }
      \widetilde\lambda_D,\\
 &c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N
   <d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D.
 \end{split} \tag{15}
\]
The two universal competitor families in (15) may be placed in one universal
quantifier block after the existential block.  Conditions (10)--(13) and
nested attainment show that at least one \(\Psi_r\) is true.  Conversely, a
solution of a \(\Psi_r\) has
\[
 c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N=\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}},
 \qquad
 d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}, \tag{16}
\]
where the second equality uses (12) and relative-interior strong duality.
Thus the finite disjunction \(\bigvee_{r=0}^d\Psi_r\) is true if and only if
the strict inequality in (10) is true.

All multiplier quantifiers can be bounded in dimension even when the equality
rows are redundant.  For a program with \(n\) primal variables, apply exact
rational row reduction to
\[
 \mathcal R:\eta\longmapsto
 \bigl(B_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta,
       d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\eta\bigr)
 \in\mathbb R^{n+1}. \tag{17}
\]
Choose columns whose images form a basis of
\(\operatorname{range}\mathcal R\).  Every multiplier has another
representative supported on those columns with the same two images in (17),
and there are at most \(n+1\leq d+1\) selected columns.  Both the exposing
identities and facial-dual feasibility and objective depend only on those two
images.  The full certificate multiplier is recovered by inserting zeros in
the unselected positions.  Therefore the existential block, including at
most \(d\) faces and exposures, has \(O(d^2)\) real variables; the combined
universal competitor block has \(O(d)\) variables.  The number of polynomial
atoms and their coefficient bit lengths are polynomial in the explicit input
length \(B\), and their degrees are bounded by a universal constant after
introducing standard auxiliary variables.  Clearing rational denominators
turns them into the integer-coefficient sign conditions required by
\texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination}.

That cited effective theorem now gives a total exact decision procedure for
the disjunction and, whenever it is true, real-algebraic sample values for all
existential variables.  Denote the sampled values again by
\(y_N,\lambda_D,y^\circ,z_k,\eta_k\).  By (15)--(16), the algebraic numbers
\[
 p_N:=c_{\mathrm{nested}}^{\top}y_N,
 \qquad
 q_D:=d_{\mathrm{deep}}^{\top}\lambda_D
\]
satisfy
\[
 p_N=\Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}},
 \qquad q_D=\Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}},
 \qquad q_D-p_N=\Delta>0. \tag{18}
\]
Exact real-algebraic arithmetic supplies square-free polynomial
representations and isolating intervals for \(p_N\) and \(q_D\).  Repeated
rational bisection, with exact polynomial sign determination at each rational
midpoint, produces outward rational enclosures \(I_N\) and \(I_D\).  Once
each interval has length less than \(\Delta/3\), (18) implies
\[
 \sup I_N
 <p_N+\frac{\Delta}{3}
 <q_D-\frac{\Delta}{3}
 <\inf I_D. \tag{19}
\]
Hence the adaptive exact test \(\sup I_N<\inf I_D\) eventually succeeds,
although the algorithm need not know \(\Delta\) in advance.  The sampled
chain, algebraic points and multipliers, and the two intervals then form the
finite \(\mathsf{GapCert}\) of \texttt{def:gap-certificate}.  This proves the
forward implication.  The reverse implication is exactly
\texttt{prop:strict-gap-sufficient}.  It also shows that, when the exact
decision procedure returns false, no valid certificate exists.

We give the promised bit bound.  By
\texttt{lem:effective-real-algebraic-elimination}, a formula with the fixed
two-block pattern above, polynomial input size, and block dimensions bounded
by a polynomial in \(d\) can be decided and sampled in at most
\[
 (B+1)^{d^{c_0}} \tag{20}
\]
bit operations after increasing a universal constant \(c_0\); the same
envelope bounds the degrees, coefficient heights, exact algebraic arithmetic,
and sign determination.  There is a universal \(\kappa_0>0\) such that
\(d^{c_0}\leq2^{\kappa_0d}\) for every positive integer \(d\).  To force the
absolute interval lengths below \(\min\{1,\Delta\}/3\), bisection needs, in
addition to the algebraic representation length, at most a polynomial number
of operations in
\[
 \ell_\Delta:=\left\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\right\rceil+1.
\]
Polynomial evaluation at the resulting rational endpoints has bit cost
polynomial in the representation length and \(\ell_\Delta\).  Absorbing
these polynomial factors and (20) by increasing a universal constant yields
\[
 \bigl(B+\lceil\log_2^+(1/\Delta)\rceil+1\bigr)^{
       2^{\kappa_{\mathrm{alg}}d}}. \tag{21}
\]
The verifier checks the face descriptions and the first-order face identities
by exact real-closed-field decision, reduces every displayed affine equality
to an exact polynomial identity in \(\mathbb A_{\mathrm{rep}}\), and uses
exact sign determination for (14), orthant signs, relative-interior signs,
and facial-dual membership.  Outward-rounded rational arithmetic is used only
to enclose the two objectives and to check the strict rational comparison in
(19).

The positive part in (21) cannot be removed under the stated input class.
Indeed, consider \(N=4\), \(T=2\), \(K=1\), and one treated unit \(j\) with
\(T_j=1\), one unit \(e\) with \(T_e=2\), and two never-treated units
\(d_1,d_2\).  Then
\[
 D_{j0}=\{e,d_1,d_2\},
 \qquad D_{j1}=\{d_1,d_2\},
 \qquad \mathcal J=\{j\}.
\]
Take \(p=1\), \(x_i=0\), and \(L=\delta=0\).  Fix the supplied admissible
positive rational \(z_B\) and its tail certificates.  For any positive
rational \(c\), let \(R_Q\) be diagonal, with entry \(c\) on every
time-\(1\) row cell and entry \(c/10\) on every time-\(2\) row cell.  This is
a full-rank rational factor with covariance eigenvalues in the legal band
\([c^2/100,c^2]\).  The cells in the two rows have different calendar times
and hence are distinct.  For \(q\) equal-variance donors, Cauchy--Schwarz
gives
\[
 \sum_{i=1}^q w_i^2\geq\frac1q,
\]
with equality at uniform weights.  Therefore the minimized squared noise
norms at horizons zero and one are, respectively,
\[
 \begin{array}{c|cc}
 &h=0&h=1\\ \hline
 \mathrm{nested}&4c^2/3&3c^2/200\\
 \mathrm{deep}&3c^2/2&3c^2/200.
 \end{array}
\]
Because the two weight coordinates vary independently and the objective is
their maximum, (8) yields
\[
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{nested}}=z_Bc\sqrt{4/3},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{\mathrm{deep}}=z_Bc\sqrt{3/2},
\]
and hence
\[
 \Delta=z_Bc\bigl(\sqrt{3/2}-\sqrt{4/3}\bigr).
\]
This gap exceeds one for all sufficiently large rational \(c\).  Thus the
model supplies no normalization forcing \(\Delta\leq1\); using
\(\log_2(1/\Delta)\) without its positive part could make the alleged
precision allowance negative even though reading and verifying the finite
input still has positive cost.

None of the arguments above invokes uniqueness, positivity of every donor
weight, predictor-column independence, ordinary Slater feasibility, or strict
complementarity.  Zero weights are ordinary orthant-boundary points,
redundant predictors only repeat polynomial conditions, and (14) together
with the explicit face encoding includes both ray faces and the zero face of
every tight or collapsed Lorentz block.  The equivalence and the construction
are finite-sample, exact statements; no limiting argument is used.
